content.text: I reviewed every input file, all draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full trace of each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement against the disclosure and the USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and checked. All 22 claims (1-12 apparatus, 13-17 apparatus, 18-22 method) were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (the conversation USER passage is a truncated duplicate and adds nothing); all 27 numerals in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) were checked for a single consistent meaning, for use in the description, and for appearance in at least one figure brief, with no orphan and no duplicate-meaning numeral; and all seven figure briefs were checked against draft/07-drawings.md and the detailed description. Supported items verified include: rail/upper and lower face/longitudinal slot through the rail; printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed-but-reversible fence at the first end secured by two screws in two corresponding mounting holes with the downwardly projecting portion moving from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the marked face still faces away from the workpiece; perpendicularity of the fence and inward extension of the rail; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages with lower keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a bore passing completely through the carriage and registering with the slot, the two bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe; a pointer on each carriage aligned with its bore axis and readable against the marks, their difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the full use sequence; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list and hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitations. Schematic depiction conventions (plain block carriages, round knobs, plain rectangular fence, generic slot and notch outlines) are confined to the figure briefs, the claims and description remain shape-neutral, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" broadening language appears in the application text. Section-line designations 3-3 and 5-5 are repeated identically in the FIG. 2 source-view brief, in the resulting FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 briefs, in draft/07-drawings.md, and in the detailed description; the abstract is under 150 words; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains. Two internal-consistency defects were verified and are reported: (1) FIG. 7 fixes the pencil centerline 94 as running lengthwise of the rail and beneath it, which combined with FIG. 1's rail spaced inward with a longitudinal side facing the workpiece edge makes the drafted step of moving the jig along the straight edge until the index and notch align with the centerline unachievable, and that motion is itself not stated in the disclosure; and (2) the straight transverse cutting planes 3-3 and 5-5 are specified as containing both the clamp-knob shank/clamping shoe and the drill-bushing bore, which must occupy the longitudinal slot at different lengthwise stations. No untraced technical assertion (structure, material, result, operating condition, or variant) was found in the description, claims, abstract, or figure briefs beyond the two items reported.

findings.title: Centerline 94 depicted as lengthwise of the rail conflicts with the drafted "move the jig along the straight edge" alignment step, which is itself not stated in the disclosure
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md (centerline 94 paragraph); draft/08-detailed-description.md (use paragraph beginning "The user marks a centerline 94"); draft/09-claims.md claim 18 (sixth step)
findings.detail: FIG. 7 fixes the pencil centerline as parallel to the rail and hidden beneath it, and FIG. 1 fixes the rail as spaced inward from the workpiece edge with a longitudinal side facing that edge (i.e., the rail lies parallel to the referenced edge). Under those two briefs the centerline is parallel to the referenced edge, so translating the jig along that edge cannot bring the transverse center index and the sight notch into or out of alignment with the centerline; the drafted step and claim 18 therefore recite a motion that cannot achieve the recited alignment. The disclosure affirmatively supports the alignment relationship itself (notch aligned with the index, and both aligned with the pencil centerline), but it never states the direction of the centerline relative to the rail, never states that the rail overlies the centerline, and never states that the jig is slid along the edge to reach the alignment; the drafter added the motion direction. Removing the added motion wording restores consistency without adding any structure and keeps the wording within the disclosure's own use sequence.
findings.evidence: FIG-7.md: "A centerline 94 is a straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone... The line runs lengthwise of the rail 10 beneath the band and emerges from beneath the second end of the rail 10 at the sight notch 26". FIG-1.md: "A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92" and "a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on the longitudinal side of the rail 10 that faces the workpiece edge 92". draft/08: "The jig is then slid along the workpiece edge 92 until the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are aligned with the centerline 94." Claim 18: "moving the drilling jig along the straight edge until the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the centerline;". Nearest disclosure passage (no affirmative support for the motion or the centerline direction): "The user places the lower face on the workpiece, presses the fence or the installed spacer plate against the selected workpiece edge, aligns the sight notch and center index with the pencil centerline, and drills through both bushings."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "The jig is then slid along the workpiece edge 92 until the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are aligned with the centerline 94." with "The sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are then aligned with the centerline 94." In draft/09-claims.md claim 18 replace "moving the drilling jig along the straight edge until the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the centerline;" with "aligning the transverse center index and the sight notch with the centerline;". Make no change to FIG. 7, which tracks the disclosed alignment of the notch, the index, and the centerline.

findings.title: Straight transverse cutting planes 3-3 and 5-5 are specified as containing both the clamp-knob shank/clamping shoe and the drill-bushing bore, which cannot lie in one transverse plane
findings.detail: The clamp-knob shank passes through the longitudinal slot into the shoe, and the drill-bushing bore registers with the same longitudinal slot; the two features must therefore be at different lengthwise stations along the slot. FIG. 2 specifies each cutting-plane line as a single straight broken line crossing the carriage transverse to the length of the rail, yet FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 each show the knob, its shank, the shoe, the key, and the bushing bore in that one section. A single straight transverse plane cannot contain both the shank/shoe and the bore. This is a drawing-convention defect only; the fix is confined to the figure briefs, changes no application text, and adds no structure, since offset (stepped) section planes with the offset shown are standard practice.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "A broken cutting-plane line 3-3 crosses the second guide carriage 70 transverse to the length of the rail 10 to establish the cross-sectional view of FIG. 3." FIG-3.md: "A threaded shank extends from the knob, through the carriage 70 and the slot 16, and into a clamping shoe 80 located below the rail 10. A cylindrical drill bushing 74 is carried by the carriage 70, its vertical bore passing completely through the carriage 70 and aligned with the slot 16." Disclosure: "A threaded shank of the knob passes through the carriage and the longitudinal slot into a clamping shoe below the rail" and "The bore passes completely through the carriage and aligns with an opening through the slot".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, specify each section line as an offset cutting-plane line: for 3-3, "A broken, offset cutting-plane line 3-3 crosses the second guide carriage 70 transverse to the length of the rail 10, the offset being shown in FIG. 2 so that the line passes through the axis of the drill bushing 74 and through the axis of the clamp knob 78"; make the corresponding change for line 5-5 with respect to the drill bushing 54 and the clamp knob 58 of the first guide carriage 50. Retain the numeral designation at each of the two ends and the existing viewing-direction arrows, and make no change to draft/07-drawings.md, the detailed description, or the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 briefs.
